claim: Let \(G=K_{n_1,\ldots,n_r}\) be a finite simple complete multipartite graph with \(r\ge2\), and let \(t_j=|\{i:n_i=j\}|\). For the Cody--Detore \(3,2\)-domination number, \[\gamma^3_2(G)=\begin{cases}N,&\text{if every }n_i=1,\\2,&\text{if }r=2\text{ or }t_2>0,\\3,&\text{otherwise,}\end{cases}\] where \(N=\sum_i n_i\). The minimum sets are completely classified: in the complete-graph case the unique minimum set is \(V(G)\); when \(r=2\), the minimum two-sets are exactly the cross-part pairs together with any whole part of order two; when \(r\ge3\) and \(t_2>0\), they are exactly the whole parts of order two; and in the remaining case the minimum three-sets are exactly a whole part of order three, a \(2+1\) selection across two parts, or, only when \(r=3\), a transversal meeting all three parts. Consequently the number of minimum sets is respectively \(1\), \(n_1n_2+t_2\), \(t_2\), or \[t_3+\sum_i\binom{n_i}{2}(N-n_i)+\mathbf 1_{r=3}\prod_i n_i.\]

correctness.rationale: For an outside vertex in part \(V_i\), every relevant witness is a length-two geodesic. Exhausting whether the outside vertex is an endpoint or the middle gives the exact local criterion. Applying it to all set-size two and three occupancy profiles proves the value, classifies every minimum set, and gives the count. An independent adjacency-based exhaustive verifier agrees on all 87 complete-multipartite types through order 9.

value.rationale: The initiating paper expressly asks for k,d-invariants of complete multipartite graphs. This theorem gives a complete exact answer for the first genuinely geodesic case (3,2), identifies sharp structural transitions at two parts and at parts of order two, and classifies/counts every optimum set rather than giving only the value. The result is a natural family-level solution to a stated research direction, not an arbitrary finite slice.
